key_results.quote: A top-activation probe B that shares just 13 of 254 heads with the single-bucket set A, a Jaccard of 0.03, produces a BOS-context effect at least as large at both scales

key_results.quote: All four Pythia checkpoints show clean positive selectivity on both corpora, all eight CIs strictly excluding zero

limitations_stated_by_authors.quote: The intervention grid covers four Mamba checkpoints (Mamba-1 130M / 2.8B, Mamba-2 1.3B / 2.7B) on wikitext-2 (Merity et al., 2017) and Pile-10k (Gao et al., 2020); the 30-seed cross-dataset confirmation covers all 8 M-2 head-granularity headline cells.

limitations_stated_by_authors.text: Hybrid SSM-attention models out of scope

formal-task evaluations (parity, Dyck-2, S3 -permutation) are deferred.

limitations_stated_by_authors.text: Untested token classes may carry additional causal sets
limitations_stated_by_authors.quote: Untested classes, including punctuation and whitespace_word, may carry additional causal sets.

limitations_stated_by_authors.text: Small Mamba-2 effect sizes and wide CI
limitations_stated_by_authors.quote: Mamba-2 single-bucket differentials are small (+0.25–+2.48 on BOS-context vs. +3.76 for M-1 130M); the M-2 1.3B gate_one CI is wide but excludes zero.
The headline bootstrap CIs resample the 30 complement seeds and condition on the fixed probe-selected set; they do not propagate document-sampling or specialist-selection uncertainty.

limitations_stated_by_authors.text: NIAH complement is single random draw
limitations_stated_by_authors.quote: The NIAH complement is a single random draw, not a multi-seed control.

threats_not_stated_by_authors: The non-uniqueness result is specific to Mamba-2 head-shared ∆ gating; it may not transfer directly to Gemma 4 E2B KV-shared layers, where the sharing mechanism and intervention surfaces differ.
Probe-selected specialist sets are defined on wikitext-2 and transferred unchanged; selection uncertainty is not propagated, so causal effect estimates may be conditional on one probe definition.
The RULER NIAH evidence uses 30 trials per condition and a single random complement draw, limiting reliability and generalization of the retrieval-collapse claim.
gate_zero and u_zero are identical output knockouts, so the paper cannot identify the mediating pathway between head output and loss; output ablation may disrupt multiple mechanisms.
The Pythia cross-architecture comparison uses a different specialist threshold semantics (attention-to-BOS > 0.10) than Mamba’s pre-softplus ∆ threshold, which may confound architecture comparisons.

The paper does not test KV-shared layers, per-layer embeddings, logit lens, induction heads, or factual-recall tracing, so relevance to the lab’s Gemma 4 E2B internals is analogical rather than direct.
data.relevance_to_lab: Directly relevant as a caution for activation-patching and logit-lens work on Gemma 4 E2B: a single probe’s top-activating units may not be the unique causal circuit, especially on head-shared or KV-shared substrates. The recommended check—run a second probe and ablate the difference sets—fits the lab’s CPU patching workflow. The intervention-surface dissociation also warns that perturbing a readout signal versus suppressing output can yield different causal conclusions for induction-head and factual-recall tracing.

data.title: A Circuit, Not The Circuit: Non-Unique Causal Localisation of the Mamba-2 State Sink
data.research_question: Does a single probe's top-activating units identify the unique causal circuit for the Mamba-2 state sink, and do representational similarity or the intervention surface predict causal function?

models_and_data.item: Mamba intervention grid: Mamba-1 130M/2.8B and Mamba-2 1.3B/2.7B.
models_and_data.quote: 4 models (Mamba-1 130M / 2.8B, Mamba-2 1.3B / 2.7B) × 6 interventions (gate_zero / gate_one / gate_mean / delta_zero / delta_median / u_zero) × 7 channel/head scopes × 6 layer scopes × 4 tasks × 3 seeds

models_and_data.item: Mamba-2 130M was used for the F1 scale ladder and cross-method phenomenology.
models_and_data.quote: Mamba-2 130M is added for the F1 scale ladder (§4.3.1) and the phenomenology cross-method correlations only.

models_and_data.item: Pythia 160M–2.8B served as the attention-head cross-architecture baseline; hybrid SSM–attention models were out of scope.
models_and_data.quote: Pythia (Biderman et al., 2023) 160M–2.8B is the cross-architecture baseline; hybrid SSM–attention models such as Zamba (Glorioso et al., 2024) are out of scope.

models_and_data.item: wikitext-2 supplied a 30-document sample for class-conditioned activation extraction and primary scoring.
models_and_data.quote: For each (layer, channel) in Mamba-1 and (layer, head) in Mamba-2, we compute mean pre-softplus activation āℓ,u,c on tokens of class c ∈ {BOS, newline, punctuation, whitespace_word} over a 30-document wikitext-2 sample

models_and_data.item: The NeelNanda/pile-10k subset supplied 30 documents per cell for cross-corpus replication with WikiText-defined sets transferred unchanged.
models_and_data.quote: Cross-dataset replication uses the NeelNanda/pile-10k subset of The Pile (Gao et al., 2020): 30 documents per cell, filtered to contain at least two newline tokens per chunk for parity with the wikitext-2 sampling.

models_and_data.item: RULER-style Needle-in-a-Haystack was evaluated at 1024 and 2048 context on two flagship Mamba checkpoints.
models_and_data.quote: We test whether the bos-specialist set transfers to a qualitatively different task by running a RULER-style Needle-in-a-Haystack (Hsieh et al., 2024) probe at 1024 and 2048 context on the two flagship Mamba checkpoints.

models_and_data.item: Phenomenological sink-mass comparisons covered all seven Mamba checkpoints.
models_and_data.quote: two prior-work metrics (Chiang et al., 2025; Ye et al., 2025) and two analytic baselines (right-tail Pr(∆pre > 0.7) and − log A from the stored Alog parameter) are evaluated per channel/head per layer for all 7 Mamba checkpoints.

protocol.step: Compute class-conditioned mean pre-softplus gate activation, subtract reference-token activation, and threshold the differential at τ = 0.5.
protocol.quote: The threshold τ = 0.5 is fixed across all 7 models and pre-registered to mark the gate’s “on” state (softplus(0.5) ≈ 0.97); values below threshold map to the low-state mode of the bimodal pre-∆ distribution (§3.3).

protocol.step: Run the pre-registered factorial intervention grid over models, interventions, scopes, layer scopes, tasks, and seeds.
protocol.quote: totalling 12,096 cells of which 6,048 are evaluated (parity and Dyck-2 task loaders deferred per pre-registration).

protocol.step: Construct 95% bootstrap intervals from 30 scored documents using 5,000 bootstrap samples.
protocol.quote: Each cell uses a 30-document bootstrap CI (nboot = 5,000).

protocol.step: Score next-token NLL on BOS-context and newline targets on both corpora.
protocol.quote: We score next-token NLL on two target classes, BOS-context (the first eight tokens after BOS) and newline (positions whose target token is a newline), each on wikitext-2 and Pile-10k.

protocol.step: Interpret intervention labels by their actual hook surface, including the retained learned bias in Mamba-2 delta_zero.
protocol.quote: In Mamba-2, delta_zero zeros the pre-softplus timestep input, leaving the post-softplus timestep set by the learned bias.

protocol.step: Compare the single-bucket probe with a size-matched top-K probe, then separately ablate their intersection and two difference sets.
protocol.quote: The single-bucket probe A and the top-K probe B are matched in size by construction (251 heads at 1.3B, 254 at 2.7B); their intersection holds 11 and 13 heads, so each difference set holds 240 and 241.

protocol.step: Hold the selected units and scored positions fixed while contrasting input-side Δ interventions with output-side knockouts.
protocol.quote: We hold the head set and the scored positions fixed and change only the intervention surface.

protocol.step: Measure retrieval using thresholded teacher-forced answer-token NLL over three needle depths.
protocol.quote: We report a thresholded teacher-forced success rate: a trial counts as retrieved when the mean answer-token NLL is below 3.0, with 10 trials at each of three needle depths (30 per condition).

metrics.name: Specialist-minus-complement differential NLL
metrics.definition: The mean NLL under specialist-unit ablation minus the mean under a size-matched random-complement ablation.
metrics.quote: We report differentials: specialist mean minus size-matched random-complement mean, since ratios are unstable when the complement is near zero.

metrics.name: Unit specialty classification
metrics.definition: A unit is classified by how many token classes exceed the activation-differential threshold.
metrics.quote: A unit is a c-specialist if exactly one class clears threshold; a dual specialist if two classes clear threshold; a generalist if three or more; silent otherwise.

metrics.name: Dual-to-single-bucket aggregate effect ratio
metrics.definition: The dual-set ablation differential divided by the single-bucket specialist differential under gate_one on BOS-context.
metrics.quote: At gate_one ablation on BOS-context at L_all, the dual set carries 4.8–6.4× the single-bucket differential on both M-2 scales and both corpora.

metrics.name: BOS–newline class-conditional cosine
metrics.definition: Cosine similarity between class-conditioned mean Δpre vectors for BOS and newline at each selected unit.
metrics.quote: Dual heads align on BOS and newline at cos = 0.89–0.90, against 0.53–0.54 for the specialists.

metrics.name: Top-10% Jaccard agreement
metrics.definition: Overlap between probe-derived bos-specialist sets and sets derived from alternative sink-mass operationalizations.
metrics.quote: The pre-registered prediction was that ≥ 3 of 4 sink-mass metrics should agree with probe-derived bos-specialist sets at top-10% Jaccard > 0.4.

metrics.name: Answer-span per-token NLL gap
metrics.definition: Increase in per-token NLL on the retrieved answer span under bos-specialist ablation.
metrics.quote: The per-token NLL gap on the answer span under bos-specialist ablation is ∼ 8.5 nats on M-1 2.8B and ∼ 9.7 nats on M-2 2.7B, substantially larger than the corresponding BOS-context differentials.

key_results.claim: At Mamba-1 channel granularity, the bos-specialist set carries a substantial causal effect.
key_results.numbers: +3.76 nats on both wikitext-2 and Pile-10k.
key_results.quote: Ablating the bos-specialist channel set across all layers (gate_zero × bos_specialist × L_all) on Mamba-1 130M produces a differential of +3.76 nats on both wikitext-2 and Pile-10k against the size-matched random complement

key_results.claim: The Mamba-2 single-bucket bos-specialist effect is positive across the headline grid.
key_results.quote: All 8 cells of the 30-seed grid (2 scales × 2 interventions × 2 corpora) show positive single-bucket bos-specialist differentials with bootstrap CI excluding zero (Table 2).

key_results.claim: Causal localisation is non-unique because a near-disjoint top-activation set matches or exceeds the single-bucket set.
key_results.numbers: 13 of 254 heads; Jaccard of 0.03; at least as large at both scales.
key_results.quote: A top-activation probe B that shares just 13 of 254 heads with the single-bucket set A, a Jaccard of 0.03, produces a BOS-context effect at least as large at both scales, so the single-bucket set is not the unique locus.

key_results.claim: The shared intersection between the two probes is active, but it cannot account for the whole causal effect.
key_results.quote: The shared core is causally active on its own, +1.02 to +3.40 across the four rows, but it does not account for the whole effect: removing it from either probe leaves a set that is still load-bearing.

key_results.claim: Representationally similar dual heads do not reproduce the bos-specialist causal profile.
key_results.quote: Dual heads, 27–35% of the total, come from the same probe under a multi-class aggregation rule and are near-collinear with the specialists on BOS and newline, yet under class-conditional ablation they do not stand in for them.

key_results.claim: The measured effect dissociates by intervention surface: perturbing the Δ signal read by the probe has little effect, whereas suppressing head output has a much larger effect.
key_results.numbers: At most 0.16 nats for Δ perturbation; 1.5 to 7.3 nats for output suppression.
key_results.quote: perturbing the input-dependent ∆ the probe reads moves the loss by at most 0.16 nats, while suppressing the same heads’ output moves it by 1.5 to 7.3 nats.

key_results.claim: The identified heads are behaviorally important for long-context retrieval.
key_results.numbers: 30/30 to 0/30 at 1024 context on both flagship checkpoints.
key_results.quote: The heads still matter behaviourally, dropping needle-retrieval success on a RULER-style probe from 30/30 to 0/30 at 1024 context on both flagship checkpoints.

key_results.claim: Pythia lacks the dense dual-head structure observed in Mamba-2.
key_results.numbers: 2–12% of heads per model on Pythia; 27–35% on Mamba-2.
key_results.quote: Applying the same multi-class rule (exactly 2 classes above threshold) to Pythia yields a sparse dual set covering only 2–12% of heads per model, against 27–35% on Mamba-2.

limitations_stated_by_authors.text: The main causal grid covers only four Mamba checkpoints and two corpora.
limitations_stated_by_authors.quote: The intervention grid covers four Mamba checkpoints (Mamba-1 130M / 2.8B, Mamba-2 1.3B / 2.7B) on wikitext-2 (Merity et al., 2017) and Pile-10k (Gao et al., 2020); the 30-seed cross-dataset confirmation covers all 8 M-2 head-granularity headline cells.

limitations_stated_by_authors.text: Three additional WikiText-2 findings did not replicate on Pile-10k.
limitations_stated_by_authors.quote: Three further wikitext-2-specific findings do not replicate on Pile-10k (Appendix D.2).

limitations_stated_by_authors.text: Formal-task evaluations were deferred, so primary evidence comes from boundary-token NLL and RULER retrieval.
limitations_stated_by_authors.quote: Primary scoring is first-eight-tokens-after-boundary NLL on BOS-context / newline plus RULER NIAH retrieval at 1024 and 2048 ctx; formal-task evaluations (parity, Dyck-2, S3 -permutation) are deferred.

limitations_stated_by_authors.text: Mamba-2 single-bucket effects are relatively small, and one 1.3B gate_one interval is wide.
limitations_stated_by_authors.quote: Mamba-2 single-bucket differentials are small (+0.25–+2.48 on BOS-context vs. +3.76 for M-1 130M); the M-2 1.3B gate_one CI is wide but excludes zero.

limitations_stated_by_authors.text: The bucketing control does not isolate head dimension, state width, or training-data alternatives.
limitations_stated_by_authors.quote: T3 rules out substrate granularity alone, not head dimension, state width, or training-data alternatives.

limitations_stated_by_authors.text: Headline intervals condition on fixed probe-selected sets and omit document-sampling and specialist-selection uncertainty.
limitations_stated_by_authors.quote: The headline bootstrap CIs resample the 30 complement seeds and condition on the fixed probe-selected set; they do not propagate document-sampling or specialist-selection uncertainty.

limitations_stated_by_authors.text: The NIAH random-complement control consists of only one draw.
limitations_stated_by_authors.quote: The NIAH complement is a single random draw, not a multi-seed control.

limitations_stated_by_authors.text: Headline confidence intervals do not include grid-wide multiple-comparison correction.
limitations_stated_by_authors.quote: Headline claims rest on the pre-registered cells of Tables 2 and 3, so we report individual 95% bootstrap CIs without grid-wide multiple-comparison correction.

threats_not_stated_by_authors: The paper does not test Gemma 4 E2B or KV-shared attention, so the Mamba-2 explanation may not transfer to layers 15–34.
Probe B is another activation-ranking probe on the same Δ-gate substrate, demonstrating non-uniqueness within one measurement family rather than under genuinely independent representations.
Because bos-specialists are selected using BOS-conditioned Δ and evaluated primarily on BOS-context NLL, shared BOS structure could partially inflate localisation despite the cross-corpus controls.
The paper's GPU and custom patched-forward implementation does not establish that equivalent Gemma activation patches will preserve numerical and hook semantics on CPU.
RULER success relies on a fixed answer-token NLL cutoff of 3.0 without reported cutoff-sensitivity analysis, so the success-rate framing may be threshold-sensitive.
Single-key RULER retrieval does not test induction, factual recall, multi-fact composition, or free-form generation, so it cannot by itself validate those lab tasks.
data.relevance_to_lab: Directly relevant as a methodological warning for Gemma 4 E2B's KV-shared layers 15–34: a per-layer embedding or logit-lens top-activation set should be treated as a candidate causal locus, not the circuit. Reuse the paper's audit by deriving a second probe, comparing intersections and difference sets under activation patching, and separating probe-read activations from output suppression before validating on induction and factual recall. The paper provides no Gemma, KV-sharing, CPU, induction-head, or factual-recall validation, so transfer remains unestablished.
